doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Getting into the University of Florida graduate program
summary: Told he lacked the background for the classical program, he registered anyway, won over the composition and trumpet professors, and ended up with a doctorate in composition.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Speaking of outside, do you think that you stand out from your classical colleagues because you’re also a jazz guy?

Okay I have to tell you the story. But the short answer is yes, is definitely yes. But see I was raising a kid myself, a son. I was in Jacksonville, Florida because I have family support there. And I was always just working at jazz, even though my undergrad stuff was classical too but I studied some at Berklee, but I was just playing jazz and knowing that I could play classical but thinking oh there’s nothing for me to do with that. So my son said to me, because I was on him about school, he said, “Well Dad, why don’t you go to school and learn something? You’re telling me about school and how important it is, what about you.” I said, “Well you know son, you’re right.” So I applied to the University of Florida for graduate school and they said, just told me, the guy told me on the phone, “Mr. Parsons, we don’t feel that you have the musical background to be successful in our legitimate music program.”

He didn’t understand who he said that to. See I’m the guy who, in 1966 I was a part of integrating a public high school in Jacksonville, Florida, in redneck Jacksonville, Florida, in one of the most redneck areas in town. And I learned how to ignore certain problems and just push on with what I’m doing anyway. So, and how to push through when I needed to. And so I drove to Gainesville the next day, that next morning, and I went to his office first and I told him that I came to register. And you know to make a long story short, I ended up registering. I bullshitted my way with the composition professor, said, “Look” – well it’s not really bullshit. I said, “You know I haven’t studied composition before but I’ve been working in jazz music and I’ve been writing music and such, you know, and if I could just take a class as a post-baccalaureate you know. And he looked at my resume and he said, “Well of course you deserve a chance, so yeah, you come on.” In fact, and he was going to put me with another composition professor and then he changed his mind and decided he would teach me himself. And then the trumpet teacher, the same thing. I got in on to take not real graduate level classes but junior level classes in trumpet and composition. So about three weeks, a month in the trumpet teacher said, “Well you know I made a mistake. You need to be in my masters program.” And she said, “Let’s take care of this right now” and went to the dean’s office and the dean came out and said, © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
“Yeah but the composition professor has already been here and says he wants you in his program.
They were vying for your attention.
Yeah. So they said, “Well here at the University of Florida we know how to do it. Tell you what, you can do both and we’ll pay for it.” Because they were so apologetic for having treated me so badly.

But it goes on. Because when the – okay the trumpet teacher was still hard on me the whole time. I mean, but I didn’t realize it. I thought this was just the normal course of study. And then after I graduated the masters I was teaching at Florida A&M and everything. The trumpet teacher had a – well I sent a student there who was being treated very nicely. I started sending students there, my graduates. And then the trumpet teacher had a stroke and insisted that I be the one to replace her at the University of Florida. So I was there just teaching classical all day, and they were so nice, they said, “Okay we won’t insult you by having you teach freshmen and sophomores, you’ll teach only upper division and graduate students. Okay? And then so I talked with the dean of the music school about maybe since I’m hanging around there maybe I could do my doctorate, finish my doctorate, because I had already started the classes before I got the job at FAMU. I had started on the doctorate in composition. So anyway, I – while I was teaching there I started taking composition with the head composition guy just to kind of get acquainted, and the University of Florida accepts one person into a doctorate of composition program per year. Only one. And they accepted me. So I commuted from Tallahassee to Gainesville to do this. But what I’m getting at is, see I’m the guy who they said couldn’t do that, so therefore being the kind of butt hole that I am I had to make sure that I was the best at that, like my daddy said.
